blockNote: Core system loop and CPU interrupt vectors.

Contains the SNES reset vector (emulation → native mode switch), the COP/NMI/IRQ vectors, the hardware initialization and boot sequence (SystemInit), and the main game loop that runs the per-frame subsystems: VBlank sync, scene management, actor processing, sprite composition, camera scrolling, HUD update and the music-upload hook.
Also provides three context-specific frame update variants (all re-entrant, callable from COP handlers and from the NMI):
- UpdateFrameDialogue: lightweight update during text/dialogue display
- UpdateFrameRender: render-only update (sprite sort/compose, HDMA reset, HUD, cutscene thinkers) for menus and transitions
- UpdateFrameFull: complete subsystem tick run from inside the NMI handler while the main loop is blocked in a music upload (musicTransitionState > 0)

The NMI handler manages VRAM DMA (scroll registers, dirty tilemap strips, CGRAM, OAM, the partial BG3 upload, then either the player tiles or the normal queued writes), reads the joypad auto-read result and sends the queued SFX byte to the SPC.

UpdateHUD runs the heads-up display: HP recovery animation (every 8th frame), stat dirty-checking (HP, max HP, gems) with a BG3 redraw, and the enemy health bar timer (a 60-frame hold, then the bar is cleared; the 25- and 30-frame values stored along the way are overwritten at once). UpdateFrameCounters maintains the invincibility timer and the capped global frame timer.
Utility routines: scroll register upload with layer priority support and the one-shot VRAM DMA (ExecuteVramDma). FillWramBlock/WramFillConstant (an OAM fill) have no caller in extracted/.

SystemInit: Full system boot sequence and main game loop.

UpdateFrameDialogue: Lightweight frame update called during dialogue and text display.

Saves and restores the full register context (B, A, X, Y, D) so it can be called re-entrantly from COP script handlers. Runs RunActors_CutsceneOnly, the OAM terminator, depth sort, camera scroll for both layers, ResetHdmaState, the type-D thinkers and sprite composition, then clears displayModeFlags bit 3 (player-tile DMA pending) so the NMI of this frame does the normal VRAM path, waits for VBlank and runs the type-C thinkers. It skips the full actor AI pass and the warp/chest checks of the main loop.
UpdateFrameRender: Minimal frame update for render-only contexts such as menus and screen transitions.

Saves the full register context. Runs only SortActorsByDepth, ComposeAllSprites, ResetHdmaState, the type-D thinkers, UpdateHUD, the VBlank sync and the type-C thinkers. Does not run actor AI, camera scrolling or the OAM terminator; the caller is expected to have handled those.
UpdateFrameFull: Complete single-frame update run from inside the NMI handler while the main loop is blocked in a music upload.

NmiHandler calls it when musicTransitionState is positive, i.e. while LoadMusicFromTransitionState is running SpcBlockTransfer with NMI enabled. Runs the type-C thinkers, RunActors_OverlayOnly, the OAM terminator, depth sort, camera scroll for both layers, ResetHdmaState, the type-D thinkers and sprite composition, between EnableNmiOnly/VBlankPartial and EnableNmiAndJoypad, so the screen keeps animating during the transfer.
UpdateHUD: Manages the in-game heads-up display for HP, gems and enemy health.

Returns at once if $09ED bit 6 (HUD off) is set. displayModeFlags bit 0 (full BG3 upload request) is saved on entry and restored on exit, so the BG3 redraw scripts below do not leave a full upload pending; the HUD uses the partial upload (bit 4) instead.
- Skipped when playerStateByte bit 1 (game over, playerFlags bit 9) is set, off an 8-frame boundary, or when hpToHeal is 0
- Decrements hpToHeal and increments playerHp (the displayed HP) toward playerMaxHp, playing sound $0D on each tick; stops when HP equals max HP
- Compares HP, max HP and gem count with the cached previous values
- On any change: sets displayModeFlags bit 4 (partial BG3 upload), counts the hundreds digit of the gem count by repeated subtraction of 100, and redraws the counters with a BG3 console script
- When enemyHpPending is nonzero: draws the bar and sets enemyHealthTimer to 60 (the $19 stored first is overwritten)
- Otherwise the timer counts down; at 0 the displayed enemy HP is cleared and the bar redrawn at once (the $1E stored first is overwritten by the STZ, so there is no separate fadeout phase)
Finally caches HP, max HP and gems for the next frame's change detection and restores displayModeFlags bit 0.

SpcTransferMusicData: Transfer music data to the SPC700 audio processor.

Continues the handshake from SpcCheckMusicReady. Sends $F0 (transfer-start), yields, and verifies zero echo. Then sends $FF (ready-for-data) and copies the music ID from chatPtr into musicTransitionState ($06FA).

Waits for musicTransitionState to become $FFFF, which the main loop's LoadMusicFromTransitionState writes after the blocking block transfer completes. Once confirmed, sends a final $01 acknowledgment, yields, clears sfxQueueCh1 and musicTransitionState, and terminates via COP Die.
The actor yields between protocol steps, so only the block transfer itself blocks the main loop.
LoadMusicFromTransitionState: Resolve a music ID and start the SPC block transfer.
Called once per main-loop iteration from SystemInit's loop, after UpdateHUD. Returns at once if musicTransitionState is zero or negative (no pending music change).

For a positive value (the track ID staged by SpcTransferMusicData) it computes the music_array index as ID × 3 (3-byte entries: 2-byte address + 1-byte bank) and loads the address and bank into direct page ($46/$47) and the shadow registers ($0687/$0688).

Enables NMI and joypad, calls SpcBlockTransfer to send the music data to the SPC700, then re-enables NMI-only mode and sets musicTransitionState to $FFFF to signal completion to the waiting SpcTransferMusicData actor. The transfer blocks the main loop; during it the NMI runs UpdateFrameFull each frame (musicTransitionState is positive).

blockNote: SRAM save/load system — game-state persistence with dual-checksum validation (252182–252392, Bank 03).
Provides the save slot infrastructure. Four save slots are supported, each occupying 512 bytes of SRAM at $306200 + (slot × 512): 508 bytes of data followed by two checksum words at +$1FC and +$1FE.
=== SAVE/LOAD ===

SaveGameState_Scene copies 508 bytes of WRAM ($0A00–$0BFB) to SRAM after storing the current scene ID at $0B06. LoadGameState_Scene reverses the process after verifying integrity. Both routines mask the slot number to 0–3 and compute the SRAM offset via XBA + ASL (slot × 256 × 2 = slot × 512).

The saved range is named eventFlags ($0A00) but holds more than event flags: it also contains the player stats and inventory state the engine keeps in that page (e.g. abilityBitmask $0AA2, playerMaxHp $0ACA, playerHp $0ACE, gemCount $0AD6) and the hieroglyph plate slots ($0B28–$0B32).
=== INTEGRITY VERIFICATION ===
ComputeSaveChecksum generates two checksums over each slot's 508 bytes (254 words):
- Additive checksum ($0018): running sum of all data words
- XOR checksum ($001C): running XOR of all data words

Both are seeded with the constant $3652, so a zeroed slot computes $3652/$3652 and never matches the stored zeros. Both are order-independent, so swapped words go undetected; the pair mainly guards against corrupted or missing data.
=== SLOT MANAGEMENT ===
ClearSaveSlot fills an entire 512-byte slot with zeros, erasing both the data and the stored checksums, so LoadGameState_Scene fails the checksum compare (carry set).
Load returns carry CLEAR on success, carry SET on failure (corrupt or empty). ClearSaveSlot returns carry SET to match the empty-slot convention.

SaveGameState_Scene: Save current game state (WRAM $0A00–$0BFB plus the scene ID) to an SRAM save slot.
Slot number passed in A (masked to 0–3). Computes the SRAM offset as (slot & 3) × 512 via XBA + ASL.
First stores the current scene number (sceneCurrent → $0B06) so it is part of the saved data. Then copies 508 bytes ($01FC) from $0A00 to SRAM at $306200 + offset.
Calls ComputeSaveChecksum and stores the additive checksum at $3063FC and the XOR checksum at $3063FE (+ slot offset). Both are verified on load.
ComputeSaveChecksum: Compute dual checksums over SRAM save data for integrity verification.
Operates on $00FE words (254 entries = 508 bytes) starting at $306200,X where X is the pre-computed slot offset.
Two running accumulators, both seeded with $3652 (non-zero, so a zeroed slot does not match its stored zero checksums):
- $0018: additive checksum — sum of all data words
- $001C: XOR checksum — running XOR of all data words
Both are order-independent, so swapping two words is not detected. Uses DP $0018, $001C and $000E as scratch.

blockNote: COP handlers for smooth interpolated movement, grid snapping, proximity testing and RNG (Bank $00, 9 COP handlers + 10 internal subroutines).

BranchIfActorNear/BranchIfPlayerNear test a square box: both |ΔX| and |ΔY| must be ≤ radius × 16 px (the code compares against radius × 16 + 1). BranchIfActorNear has no call site in extracted/. ResolveActorIndex converts an 8-bit actor list index to a WRAM pointer ($1000 + index × $30).

MoveToward is a yielding handler that moves the actor to the target in moveXAlt/moveYAlt (set up by the calling script) at a speed given in px/frame: frames = larger-axis distance ÷ speed (UnsignedDivide), stored +1 as the tick limit. Each tick it computes the offset travelled so far per axis (tick × distance ÷ frames), subtracts what was already applied, and hands the signed difference to ApplyMovement through moveScratch1/2. Distances are capped at $FE per axis, and when the distance is smaller than the speed the quotient is 0 and the actor does not move (OQ-56). InitSmoothMovement does the first-entry setup and sets extendedFlags bit 1; MoveTowardFinish clears it.

The hardware math pipeline uses chained helpers: MultiplyThenDivide feeds WRMPYB → RDMPYL → WRDIVL → RDDIVL for the cumulative offset, with ReadMultiplyResult (1 NOP) and ReadDivideResult (5 NOPs) providing the hardware latency delays. MovementVelocityCompute wraps the same pipeline for TickMove's per-axis calculations.
SnapToGrid yields to EnemyPositionSnap until the actor aligns to the 16×16 tile grid. ResumeAfterSnap restores the script pointer from snapResumePtr.

StageMove/TickMove split the same interpolation into a setup COP and a per-frame COP. StageMove reads animation, speed and a duration-cap operand, stores |dx|, |dy|, the two sign bits (animScratch2 bits 14/15) and the frame count, and halves both distances via HalveMovementDistance until the larger fits in a byte; each halving adds one extra pass, handled by TickMoveComplete. A speed operand ≥ $80 is negated to |speed| and also triggers one more halving pass (the BCC after the divide tests the carry left by CMP #$80), roughly halving the speed (OQ-55).

RngByte steps a 16-byte additive generator ($0410–$041F: each byte += the next byte + carry, then a ripple counter is incremented); it is not an LFSR. RngMod reduces the last RngByte output by repeated subtraction (a modulus of 0 would hang).
CameraScrollStepLookup reads scroll speed entries from scrollStepTableBase for the four CameraPan COP handlers in cop_handlers_effects.

BranchIfActorNear: COP #20 with one byte (actor list index), one byte (radius) and one &Code operand. Resolves the actor via ResolveActorIndex ($1000 + index × $30) and branches if both |ΔX| and |ΔY| are ≤ radius × 16 px (the code compares against radius × 16 + 1); otherwise skips the branch address.
No script in extracted/ uses this COP.
BranchIfPlayerNear: COP #21 with one byte (radius) and one &Code operand. Shares the square proximity test of BranchIfActorNear but compares against playerActor.
MoveToward: COP #22 with two byte operands (animation index, speed in px/frame). The target is in moveXAlt/moveYAlt, set by the script beforehand.

On first entry InitSmoothMovement computes the distances and the frame count and sets extendedFlags bit 1; each later call moves the actor by the next per-axis delta and yields RTL until the tick counter ($24) reaches the limit (frames + 1). Usage in extracted/: speeds 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8.
MultiplyThenDivide: Chained hardware multiply→divide giving the offset travelled by this tick.

WRMPYA holds the tick counter ($24, set by the caller). Writes the axis distance byte to WRMPYB (starting the multiply), copies the product from RDMPYL into WRDIVL as the dividend, divides by animScratch2−1 (the frame count) via WRDIVB and returns the quotient in A and $0000: the cumulative pixels moved by this tick. The caller subtracts the previous accumulator to get this frame's delta. When the divisor is zero (distance < speed) the divide is skipped and 0 is returned. Called twice per MoveToward tick (X and Y).
InitSmoothMovement: Computes the interpolation setup for MoveToward on first entry.

Converts moveXAlt/moveYAlt from absolute target coordinates to distances from the current position ($14/$16), takes their absolute values, caps each at $00FE when the high byte is non-zero, and records the sign of each axis by ROR into $0004 (stored in animScratch2's high byte: bit 14 = X negative, bit 15 = Y negative). Selects the larger axis, divides it by the speed operand via UnsignedDivide to get the frame count, stores frames + 1 as the tick limit, zeroes the accumulators, tick counter and the override-chain pointers ($2C/$2E), and sets extendedFlags bit 1.
StageMove: COP #52 with three byte operands (animation index, speed, duration cap). Computes absolute distances from moveXAlt/moveYAlt vs the current position, records the sign bits in animScratch2 (bit 14 = X negative, bit 15 = Y negative), halves both distances while the larger exceeds one byte (counting passes in chatPtr), divides the larger distance by |speed| for the frame count (+1, ORed into animScratch2) and initializes TickMove state before the RTI continuation.

Speed ≥ $80 is negated and also adds one halving pass (see the file note). The third operand goes to animScratch+3 and is $FF in all 32 uses; TickMove skips its countdown when bit 7 is set, so $FF means no cap.
RngByte: COP #23 with no operands. Steps a 16-byte additive generator over $0410–$041F and returns the new $0410 byte in A.

For X = 15..1: byte[$040F+X] += byte[$0410+X] + carry (one carry chain, so $041E += $041F first and $0410 += $0411 last). Then a ripple counter at $041F is incremented, carrying toward lower addresses. rngState ($040F) is the index base; $040F itself is never touched.
RngMod: COP #24 with one byte operand (modulus). Reduces the current RngByte output ($0410) by repeated subtraction and stores the remainder in rngModuloResult ($0420). Does not advance the generator.
A modulus of 0 would loop forever (the subtraction never goes negative); extracted/ uses $50 and $60.

blockNote: Camera scroll actor definitions and shared subroutines (Bank 00).

Defines four actor-based camera scroll behaviors used during gameplay and cutscenes. Each actor sets bit 12 ($1000) of its status word ($12; the meaning of that bit was not verified) and then computes per-frame scroll deltas with the hardware multiply/divide unit (MulDivide).

Spawn parameters: the X/Y bytes of the actor-spawn entry are not positions. The spawner makes them pixel coordinates (tile × 16); TileAlignCoord then packs each into (page << 8 | tile) and ComputeScrollDeltas passes it to MulDivide as the packed operand: low byte = multiplier, high byte = divisor. Zero skips the axis. Spawn bytes seen in extracted/: #11 (most common), #21, #41, #00, #DF (Init only). The −8 px X offset makes the X multiplier one less than the Y one for the same spawn byte (OQ-57).
The four scroll modes are:

- ScrollCameraInit: aligns both coordinates, runs the delta computation 3 times (identical inputs), copies the Y delta to effectScrollV, then computes once more and moves cameraDeltaX (bit 15 set) into forcedScrollOverride, zeroing cameraDeltaX. Used only with spawn #DF, #DF.
- ScrollCameraTrack: aligns once, then recomputes both deltas every frame.
- ScrollCameraVertical: aligns once, then recomputes only the Y delta every frame (X ignored).
- ScrollCameraAccumulate: recomputes both deltas every frame and adds the accumulators in DP $24/$26 (zeroed at start, writable by other actors).
Shared subroutines:
- TileAlignCoord: packs a pixel coordinate into (page << 8 | tile): LSR ×4 in 8-bit mode shifts only the low byte, the high byte is kept, then AND #$0F0F. Result in Y.
- TileAlignPosition: applies TileAlignCoord to X ($14, after subtracting 8) and Y ($16).
- ComputeScrollDeltas: for each axis, MulDivide(A = packed ratio from $14/$16, Y = cameraTargetX/Y) → cameraDeltaX/Y; an axis whose packed value is 0 is skipped and keeps its previous delta.

ScrollCameraInit: Camera initialization scroll actor (spawn #DF, #DF; Mt. Kress scenes).
Sets bit 12 ($1000) in the actor status word, subtracts 8 px (X) and 16 px (Y) from the position parameters and packs both with TileAlignCoord into the multiplier/divisor words $14/$16.
Runs COP LoopStart with count 3 around ComputeScrollDeltas; all three passes use the same inputs, so they give the same result. After the loop, copies cameraDeltaY to effectScrollV ($0690).

Then sets the re-entry point (COP SetEntryHere), computes the deltas again each frame, ORs bit 15 into cameraDeltaX and stores it in forcedScrollOverride ($06C8), and zeroes cameraDeltaX. Outside visual_effect_pipeline no reader of $06C8 was found in extracted/ (OQ-57).
ScrollCameraTrack: Sets bit 12 of the status word, packs the spawn position via TileAlignPosition, then re-runs ComputeScrollDeltas every frame (after COP SetEntryHere) with the current camera targets.
The default camera actor: about 100 scene spawns use it (87 of them with #11, #11).
ScrollCameraVertical: Vertical-only camera tracking actor-def referenced from scene_actors in Edward's Castle, Itory, Incan Ruins and Dao.

Sets bit 12, packs the position via TileAlignPosition, then every frame computes only the Y delta through MulDivide when $16 is nonzero. cameraDeltaX is left unchanged and the X parameter ($14) is ignored. Three of its spawns use #21, #00, whose Y parameter is 0, so they compute nothing (OQ-57).
ScrollCameraAccumulate: Accumulative camera scroll actor-def used in Pyramid interior scenes.

Zeroes the accumulators at DP $24 (X) and $26 (Y), packs the position via TileAlignPosition, then each frame calls ComputeScrollDeltas and adds the accumulators to cameraDeltaX and cameraDeltaY. Other actors can write $24/$26 to add drift on top of the standard tracking.
TileAlignCoord: Packs a pixel coordinate into (page << 8 | tile).

In 8-bit accumulator mode LSR ×4 shifts only the low byte (÷ 16, the tile index within a 256-px page); the hidden high byte (the page) is untouched. After returning to 16-bit mode, AND #$0F0F keeps the low nibble of each byte, and the result is transferred to Y for the caller to store.
TileAlignPosition: Applies TileAlignCoord to both position parameters.

Subtracts 8 px from X ($14) before packing; Y ($16) is packed as is. The packed words are stored back to $14/$16, where ComputeScrollDeltas uses them as the multiplier (low byte) and divisor (high byte) for MulDivide.
ComputeScrollDeltas: Computes the scroll delta for both axes with the hardware multiply/divide unit.

For each axis: A = the packed ratio in $14 (X) or $16 (Y), Y = cameraTargetX ($06BE) or cameraTargetY ($06C2); calls hardware_math.MulDivide via JSL, which returns (A low byte × Y) ÷ A high byte, and stores it in cameraDeltaX ($06C0) or cameraDeltaY ($06C4).
If the packed value is 0 the MulDivide call and the store are skipped and that axis keeps its previous delta.

blockNote: Scene title display system — centered area name overlay during scene transitions (172315–172521, Bank 02).

Called from ClearSceneState after actor spawning and before thinker spawning and palette loading. Displays the current scene's area name (e.g. 'South Cape', 'Edward's Castle') in a one-row dialogue box, giving the player a visual cue of the new location.
=== DISPLAY PIPELINE (DisplaySceneTitle) ===

1. Scene change guard: compares $0D6E (the scene just left, recorded by ExecuteSceneTransition; for a world-map entry it is the deferred destination) against sceneCurrent ($0644). If they are equal (a reload of the same scene ID) the title is suppressed.

2. Width measurement: CountTitleGlyphs walks the scene title wide-string at [$3E], counting visible characters while expanding dictionary references ($D6/$D7) and cursor advances ($CC). Returns the glyph count in $00.
3. Empty title guard: if the count is zero the routine returns immediately.

4. Centering: (18 − glyphCount), forced even by AND $FE, used as a byte offset into the VRAM write buffer, i.e. (18 − N) / 2 tile cells. 18 is presumably the interior of the 10-column box if a column is 2 tiles wide (inferred; there is no clamp for N > 18, OQ-58).

5. Box setup: sets $00B4 = $E0 (nonzero flag that makes ExecuteSceneTransition wait for a button press) and clears $00B5. Opens the box via scene_title_box_format ([DLG:7,7][SIZ:A,1]), i.e. a DialogStringRenderer OpenDialogueBox command with width $0A and height 1 at position (7, 7).
6. Centered render: adds the padding to the VRAM write cursor ($0998), then calls DialogStringRenderer a second time with the title string pointer.
=== GLYPH COUNTING (CountTitleGlyphs) ===
A specialized wide-string character counter for the commands found in scene title strings:
- Literal tiles (< $C0): 1 glyph each
- $CA (Return): ends the count
- $CC (AdvanceCursor): adds the operand byte to the count
- $D6/$D7 (DictionaryA/B): looks up the word in dialog_dictionary_a/b and counts each expanded character up to its $CA terminator
- Other commands (≥ $C0): skips one operand byte without counting
The scan starts at [$3E] + 1; the first string byte is skipped (assumed to be a type/length byte).
